A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, determine which represented billed revenue is tied to counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant contractual conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with source-native identifiers and invoice facts.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Only authoritative files in this data room.

required_output_shape.identifier_rendering: Report invoice_id, contract_id, and billed_name as they appear in sources (no canonical renaming in the output artifact).

world_eligible: Invoice exists with amount, currency, period, status, and billed name as recorded in billing sources.
Contract exists and is identifiable by source-native contract identifier.
Contract text contains or lacks specific clause types (change-of-control consent/notice, change-of-control termination right, assignment consent/notice/restriction) as grounded in contract sources.
Contract temporal/status facts (e.g., whether a statement of work is expired) as grounded in contract sources.
purpose_scoped: Whether a contract counts as active for this purpose (purpose applies an active-contract filter; an expired statement of work is not active).
Whether a clause type is acquisition-relevant for this purpose (purpose-defined taxonomy of CoC and assignment conditions).
Whether an invoice qualifies for inclusion (must pass active-contract and acquisition-clause filters).
Whether invoice and contract counterparty are associated as asserted vs unresolved for this report.

epistemic_requirements: Ground every persistent semantic assertion in source evidence; do not invent closed-world negation.
If a billed name and a contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, state unresolved rather than omitting the invoice or asserting the join.
Missing identity or missing association evidence is not a negative contractual finding.
Do not globally merge or split identities in service of this purpose; rely on compiled identity judgments where needed.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Invoice-to-contract/counterparty linkage cannot be confidently established from available evidence.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Include every invoice that satisfies the purpose-specific active-contract and acquisition-relevant-clause filters.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: For each included invoice, populate amount, currency, period, status, contract_id (when known), and association disposition.
completeness_expectations.sorting: Complete invoice list sorted by invoice_id.
completeness_expectations.non_goals: No requirement to enumerate invoices that fail acquisition-relevance or inactive-contract filters.

acquisition_relevant_conditions: Require consent or notice on a change of control.
Permit termination upon a change of control.
Require consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or prohibited to a competitor.
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_policy: An expired statement of work is not an active contract for inclusion.
purpose_specific_policies.inclusion_rule: Row appears only when the governing contract is active under this purpose's policy and contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition.

association_dispositions.unresolved: Association not confident; must not be treated as absence of exposure.

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, reconcile represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts; report pairwise identity judgments required to connect commercially relevant records.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Only authoritative files in this data room.

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort links by left ascending, then right ascending.

world_eligible: Distinct source records exist with stable source-native identifiers in CRM, billing, registry, and contracts.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be mechanically equivalent as a compilation fact.
Registry rows represent distinct legal entities even when trade names are similar.
purpose_scoped: Whether two records are confidently the same legal counterparty (SAME_ENTITY).
Whether two records are confidently not the same legal counterparty (DISTINCT).
Which pairwise links are required to connect CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry entity for each commercially relevant relationship.

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical equivalence; similar trade names across distinct registry entities are not automatic merges.
Missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (distinct) judgment.
SAME_ENTITY and DISTINCT require establishing evidence, not mere compatibility or absence of proof.
Explicit unresolved identity is permitted and must be recorded rather than forced.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Insufficient evidence to assert same legal counterparty or distinct entities.

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: Include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship.
completeness_expectations.pair_orientation: Emit directed left/right pairs per schema; cover required connectivity without claiming global transitive closure.
completeness_expectations.sorting: Complete link list sorted by left, then right.

purpose_specific_policies.merge_policy: No global deduplication on string similarity alone.
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_equivalence: Permit treating exact legal-form variants of the same registered name as the same entity without extended reasoning.
purpose_specific_policies.negative_judgment_policy: Absence of SAME_ENTITY evidence must not default to DISTINCT.
purpose_specific_policies.required_connectivity: For each commercially relevant relationship, link CRM ↔ billing ↔ contract ↔ registry candidates as needed.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under purpose-defined relationship and obligation criteria.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Only authoritative files in this data room.
exclusions: Expired-only or purely historical one-off relationships without current commercial tie

required_output_shape.identifier_forms: Same as Purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:).
required_output_shape.ordering: Sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row.

world_eligible: Invoice open/closed status as recorded in billing sources.
Contract contains exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term language as grounded in contract text.
Contract active vs expired status as grounded in contract sources.
Identity links between invoice-side and contract-side counterparties (may inherit UNRESOLVED from identity reconciliation).
purpose_scoped: Whether a counterparty is commercially dependent under the conjunction of current-relationship and obligation-kind tests.
Whether a current commercial relationship exists for this purpose (open invoice OR active contract with auto-renew or rolling term).
Whether dependency is reported as dependent vs unresolved when identity needed for the join is unresolved.
Which obligation_kinds apply among exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term.

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report dependency as unresolved rather than false.
Do not treat unresolved identity as evidence of non-dependency.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency under this purpose.
A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish current dependency.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Dependency cannot be confidently assessed, typically because counterparty identity linking invoice and contract is unresolved.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Include dependencies for counterparties/contracts that meet or may meet the dependency criteria; unresolved rows when identity blocks assessment.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: For each row, populate counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids (possibly empty), obligation_kinds (sorted subset of vocabulary), and status.
completeness_expectations.sorting: Complete dependency list sorted by contract_id.

purpose_specific_policies.dependency_definition: Commercially dependent when BOTH hold: (1) current commercial relationship, AND (2) active contract contains exclusivity, term auto-renewal, or rolling term continuing unless notice.
current_relationship_tests: At least one open invoice for the counterparty/relationship, OR
An active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term.
exclusions: Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
One-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create current dependency.
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_policy: Active contract means not expired; aligns with contract-source temporal facts interpreted for ongoing commercial effect.
purpose_specific_policies.identity_dependency: Uses Purpose B identifier forms and identity judgments; unresolved identity forces status unresolved, not dependent=false.
